facts.fact: The speaker presents browser-tabs (browser tabs CLI), an open-source command-line tool he built to open and organize browser tabs into named groups, to prepare Codely's weekly news livestream ("el café con Codely").
facts.trap: Describes it as a browser extension, an MCP server, or a review of someone else's tool.
facts.note: Captions write "codely"; the company is Codely. The speaker is Javi (Codely).

evidence.quote: os presento aquí ni más ni menos que browser tabs CLI, una utilidad de CLI

facts.fact: It talks directly to Vivaldi's API (the browser he uses for the show) to batch-open tabs from a JSON file in about a second, naming tabs and groups and setting colors, instead of slow AI computer use that clicks through the browser and blocks it.
facts.trap: Says it works with Firefox or Chrome, or that it uses AI/computer use to open the tabs.

evidence.quote: está tirando por las API por la API directamente de Vivaldi para poder hacer esto

facts.fact: The motivation is the tedious weekly work of opening all the news links, renaming and grouping them; automating it with AI computer use was too slow and blocked the browser.

evidence.quote: es un trabajo que cada semana hay que hacer de abrir todos los enlaces, ponerle un nombrecito, agruparlos

facts.fact: The tool is open source (MIT, on npm and GitHub), vibe-coded, and uses semantic-release (instead of release-please, which Codely used before) to publish releases automatically from conventional commits.
facts.trap: Says it uses release-please, or that it is paid/closed source.

evidence.quote: veníamos usando tradicionalmente para las distintas librerías release please y es curioso porque simplifica bastante el tinglado esto

facts.fact: He concludes the time was worth it: he learned things (badges, semantic-release, Agent Browser differences) and the tool will save him a lot of time every week.
facts.trap: Says he concluded it wasn't worth the effort.

evidence.quote: ahora esto nos va a servir de base para ahorrarme mucho tiempo cada semana
